sections.heading: Make your next move about the work
sections.lead: A title is a starting point, not a complete explanation of the value you bring.
paragraphs: A strong career conversation begins with the decisions, responsibilities, and working conditions you want to take on. Consider the kind of organization, scope, mandate, and leadership relationships that make sense for your next step. Then connect that direction to evidence from your own experience rather than relying on a title to make the case.

KOV's candidate-side support can help organize this thinking into a practical positioning and search plan. Work is scoped with you, and you remain responsible for the decisions about which opportunities to pursue and what information may be shared.
bullets: Clarify the role and mandate you want before preparing application materials.
Separate responsibilities you owned from work shared with colleagues or a governing body.
Use evidence that you can explain and substantiate.
Set boundaries around location, working arrangements, confidentiality, and timing.

sections.heading: Explore the current role guide
paragraphs: The available guide focuses on CEO career representation. It explains how to define a leadership mandate, organize evidence, prepare executive documents, consider target organizations, and decide what support to request. It is a practical starting point for candidates considering a chief executive path, not a substitute for role-specific advice about a particular employer.
As you read, note the questions that matter to your situation. A consultation can help you discuss fit, priorities, and whether KOV's services align with the support you are considering.

sections.heading: How KOV's support takes shape
paragraphs: The work begins with a discussion of your goals, constraints, and the services that may fit. For private career representation, KOV describes a process that can include assessment, target-company strategy and research, professional positioning, approved outreach, and follow-up. The specific scope and approvals are agreed before work begins. Source: KOV Career Agency.

Individual services are available for professionals who need focused help with career direction or particular materials. These may include resume or CV writing, LinkedIn profile optimization, career documents, portfolio development, personal career websites, positioning, and coaching. Select the work that addresses a defined need rather than assuming every service is necessary.

rows: Goals, background, constraints, and service fit
Whether the proposed support is relevant
Target direction, strengths, and career evidence
How to describe your experience accurately
Agreed documents, research priorities, and outreach materials
What is ready to share and with whom
Responses, interview preparation, or offer questions as applicable
Whether to proceed, pause, or decline

sections.heading: Documents that support your direction
paragraphs: Career materials should make it easier for a reader to understand your background and assess relevance to a specific opportunity. Start with the facts: roles, dates, scope, contributions, and outcomes you can support. Use clear language, explain context where needed, and avoid implying that you had authority or achieved results that belonged to a larger team.

KOV's individual career services include support for resumes and CVs, LinkedIn profiles, career documents, portfolios, and personal career websites. The appropriate deliverable depends on your objective and the work agreed with KOV. You review personal materials and retain control over whether and where they are used.

sample.heading: A generic example of clearer career writing
sample.before: Responsible for business improvement and team leadership.
sample.after: Led a cross-functional improvement initiative, clarifying decision ownership and tracking agreed operational measures.

bullets: Confirm facts and figures before including them.
Distinguish personal contribution from collective outcomes.
Adapt emphasis to the opportunity without changing the underlying facts.
Keep sensitive employer, colleague, and client information out of public-facing material.

sections.heading: Keep outreach considered and controlled
paragraphs: Professional outreach should reflect an agreed purpose and an appropriate level of disclosure. Before any contact, discuss the audience, the information that may be shared, and how a response should be handled. KOV's service description refers to approved outreach and follow-up; the candidate remains involved in decisions about fit and next steps.

If confidentiality is important, explain the constraints early. Agree how to refer to your background, which details must remain private, and how to handle a conversation that moves faster than expected. Do not assume that a recipient will treat an unsolicited message as confidential.

sections.heading: Prepare for conversations and decisions
paragraphs: Interview preparation can help you present relevant examples, describe your decision-making, and ask questions about the mandate. Build a small set of accurate examples that show context, your role, the choices available, and what followed. Be ready to discuss what you learned and what you would approach differently.

If an opportunity reaches offer discussions, assess the role's responsibilities and terms against your priorities. KOV lists coaching and executive offer support among its services. The scope of any assistance is agreed with you; the employer determines its offer, and you decide whether to accept or negotiate.

tabs.name: Before an interview
tabs.text: Review the role description, choose relevant examples, prepare thoughtful questions, and decide which points need clarification.

tabs.name: During evaluation
tabs.text: Listen for the mandate, decision rights, expectations, and practical conditions. Ask for detail when an important point is unclear.

tabs.name: At offer stage
tabs.text: Compare the written terms and role scope with your priorities. Take time to understand open questions before making a decision.

sections.heading: Choose the level of support that fits
paragraphs: Some professionals want help with one specific document or a focused coaching conversation. Others are considering a broader, agreed private career representation engagement. The services page describes how KOV approaches representation; the individual services page lists focused support options. You can discuss what is relevant before deciding whether to proceed.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right role guide?
faqs.answer: Start with the work and mandate you are considering, then review the available guide for relevant questions about positioning and career support. The current role-specific guide is for CEOs.

faqs.question: Do I need private career representation to improve my documents?
faqs.answer: No. KOV also lists individual services for documents, profiles, positioning, portfolios, websites, and coaching. Discuss your needs to identify an appropriate scope.

faqs.question: Who decides whether an opportunity is right for me?
faqs.answer: You do. KOV can provide agreed candidate-side support, while you decide which opportunities to pursue and how to respond.

faqs.question: Can KOV guarantee an interview or job offer?
faqs.answer: No. Employers make hiring decisions, and KOV does not guarantee interviews, offers, employment, or timelines.

faqs.question: What should I prepare for an initial conversation?
faqs.answer: Bring a concise outline of your goals, relevant experience, constraints, and the support you are considering. You do not need to send sensitive information before discussing how it will be handled.
